newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Gaddafi slams European force, speaks of Libyan one.
newsitem.headline: Gaddafi slams European force, speaks of Libyan one.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi on Monday condemned formation of a rapid reaction force by four European countries and said Tripoli might set up its own to oppose it.

The Libyan news agency JANA said Gaddafi, in a speech to "members of the population", said the agreement by France, Italy, Spain and Portugal was "a step to break all the good relations between Arab and European countries".
He added: "Libya will probably begin to prepare a force to resist the European forces."
JANA said Gaddafi was "astonished by this agreement".
The Libyan newspaper El Jamahiria said on Monday that the formation on Saturday of the force known as Eurofor was a "declaration of war in the south Mediterranean".
Once fully operational, Eurofor will be able to call on up to 10,000 troops for use on humanitarian and peacekeeping missions. It has its command headquarters in Florence, Italy.

JANA said Libyan foreign minister Omar Mustafa al-Montasser summoned the four countries' ambassadors on Sunday evening and "informed them of the anxiety and unease of the Great Jamahiriyah (Libya)" about the agreement to set up the force.
Montasser said the agreement "could not be accepted in the 21st Century" and asked for an explanation from the four governments through their ambassadors.
Libyan television said another cabinet member met diplomats from Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia on Sunday and stressed the importance of reaching a unified stance towards the force.

The secretary for unity affairs, Jomaa al-Fezzani, told the three diplomats that Libya "totally rejects it (Eurofor) because of the dangers it entails and which threaten the independence of the Arab Maghreb Union states". The union groups Algeria, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco and Tunisia.
El Jamahiria said formation of the force signalled "a new conflict between South and North" and showed that the European countries "make light of the dignity and freedom of others".
